extracted.intended_audience: federal agency managers and budget/planning staff (Deputy Directors, Directors of Planning/Programming/Budgeting, Directorate leads)
extracted.subtask_description: Implementation and reporting requirements for agency management improvement programs under OMB Circular A-44: establish programs for management effectiveness and cost reduction, set quantitative goals and performance indicators, validate and report results, and share applicable methods Government‑wide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management improvement program elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The management improvement program will consist of five interrelated elements: (1) Management effectiveness; (2) Cost reduction; (3) Idea interchange; (4) Presidential recognition of exceptional improvement actions; (5) Periodic study of Government-wide operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must adopt all five elements as the framework for program design, reporting, and incentives; each element has specific policies, procedures, and reporting expectations described elsewhere in the Circular.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual management improvement report (timing & routing)
rubrics_metrics.description: An annual management improvement report covering the program elements will be prepared and submitted in duplicate to the President, through the Director of the Bureau of the Budget, by September 30 of each year (first report due Sept. 30, 1970).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports must follow the definitions and formats in Attachment A. Agency-level compilation is required; Directorate reports feed into the Agency report. Initial and interim reporting deadlines (e.g., initial report due dates described in Agency instructions) must be observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management effectiveness requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each department and agency head will establish a formal, organized management effectiveness program to identify priority problem areas, set quantitative goals, measure performance, evaluate results, and initiate corrective actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies to observe include: (a) establish a management system for quantitative goals and evaluation; (b) select areas assuring priority attention where greatest needs exist; (c) add or remove specific problems based on acceptability of performance; (d) report performance results as the combined effect of all management actions for that area; (e) express indicators in appropriate quantitative terms; (f) create new data bases if existing data are deficient; (g) if dollar savings result, report under cost reduction as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance indicators and measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance indicators must be significant quantitative measurements (units, tons, percentages, gross dollars, items, or other appropriate standards) that provide perspective on the total management effort applied to the problem or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting format (Exhibit 1) requires specifying performance indicators, base period reference (A = preceding fiscal year cumulative; B = June 30 of preceding fiscal year), base year data, past year data, current year data, and goals. Performance evaluation must compare actual performance against past experience and approved goals, cite actions contributing to improvement, analyze shortfalls, and state corrective actions with target dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost reduction policy (agency responsibility and approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Heads of departments and agencies assume personal responsibility for improving efficiency and economy. Management must undertake vigorous efforts to improve procedures, eliminate nonessential activities and positions, and increase productivity while accomplishing unprogrammed workload without added staff where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should adjust previously programmed requirements and improve manpower control and utilization. Emphasis on managerial actions deliberately taken to raise effectiveness or efficiency, not actions taken to carry out public policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost reduction planning (required plan content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each department and agency head will prepare specific cost reduction plans which systematically: (1) identify and eliminate or curtail marginally effective activities; (2) develop new and less costly methods of achieving program objectives; (3) encourage innovation in techniques for increasing productivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans should set both overall monetary goals and subgoals for major activities or organizational elements, and goals must be realistic and based on actual costs in the immediately preceding year or most recently incurred costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monetary goals and subgoals
rubrics_metrics.description: At the beginning of each fiscal year, department and agency heads will establish a cost reduction goal representing expected savings from new and improved management actions; agencies should also establish subgoals for major activities or organizational elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Goals must reflect savings compared with the immediately preceding year (or most appropriate recent base) and be expressed in dollars and manpower where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of monetary savings (what counts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Monetary savings reported must be the result of deliberate managerial actions taken to raise effectiveness or efficiency (new or improved management actions) and must be attributable to those actions, not to external or incidental factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit exclusions: do NOT count reductions due solely to a decline in demand for agency output; deferral of programs; transfers of functions to other agencies (except net Government savings); prevention of cost increases via voluntary uncompensated overtime; acquisition of excess property where funds for new purchases were not available; reductions based on external authority decisions; over-estimates of budgetary requirements. Only reductions attributable to new/improved management actions are reportable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement and time-phasing of reported savings
rubrics_metrics.description: Monetary savings resulting from each new or improved management action will be calculated and reported separately for three fiscal years: the year the action is taken and the two succeeding fiscal years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First-year reported savings represent funds made available or additional revenue resulting from the action; the next two years' figures estimate additional funds that would have been required had the action not occurred. Use planned or actually incurred expenditures as the base when appropriate. Past- and estimated future-year savings are dropped from the reporting system after each annual report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification, control, and disposition of savings
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency must establish controls to assure that funds made available by cost reduction actions are used only for approved programs and must identify the effect/use of past-year savings using categories: (1) used to finance other approved requirements of the reporting unit; (2) reprogrammed to another appropriation or budget activity (report anticipated use); (3) placed in reserve or applied to reducing the President's budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Savings must be reported by component, program category, sub-category and element, and reflect disposition of anticipated or actual savings to allow appropriate consideration in budget formulation and review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation of reported savings (internal validation system)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each department and agency head will establish an internal system for validation of reported savings. Validation means an independent evaluation of the reasonableness and validity of amounts reported as savings, assigned to an organization independent of the claiming unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validation should review an adequate number of individual savings actions before submission to the Bureau of the Budget; scope should balance cost of validation against potential benefits. Validation procedures should provide reasonable assurance that: (1) reported actions actually took place; (2) reported savings represent reasonable computations/estimates of savings in the year reported and result from specific new or improved management actions; (3) reported savings are net of identifiable offsetting cost increases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Idea interchange (internal and external dissemination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency should have an internal system for distributing management improvement information to its organizational elements. Externally, agencies will identify in the annual report actions considered applicable to other departments and agencies, including description, methodology, new approaches, and a point of contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptions chosen for external distribution should be concise and screened for relevance to other agencies; the Bureau of the Budget will consolidate and distribute applicable items Government-wide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program incentives and recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should use a variety of techniques to stimulate improvement (award ceremonies, certificates, publicity, symposiums, workshops, monetary awards under Incentive Awards Program). Agency heads may nominate individuals/units for Presidential recognition for exceptional improvement actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominations for Presidential recognition must include detailed descriptions of efforts and results and will be reviewed by the President's Advisory Council on Management Improvement. Recommendations for incentive awards should be submitted under the agency merit award program by specified deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic Government-wide studies and interagency coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Periodically the Bureau of the Budget will choose common operational areas for Government-wide study; an interagency steering group will coordinate the effort and produce a final report. Agencies will focus on selected areas and submit reports on accomplishments (dollar savings, actions taken, plans for future improvements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possible study areas include common administrative functions (records management, travel, communications, printing). The Bureau will notify agencies and transmit detailed instructions for each study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report format and Directorate plan sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Directorate annual plans will include four sections: Section I - Management Effectiveness Goals (upcoming fiscal year); Section II - Cost-Reduction Goals (upcoming fiscal year); Section III - Management Effectiveness Accomplishments (current fiscal year); Section IV - Cost-Reduction Accomplishments (current fiscal year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section I should cover actions/studies expected to increase efficiency where dollar quantification is unclear. Section II should cover studies/actions likely to produce measurable dollar/manpower savings, with concrete actions and realistic goals. Sections III and IV report accomplishments compared to prior year planning goals and summarize unanticipated achievements. The initial report will define areas selected for study and related goals and summarize significant past-year projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit 1 reporting fields and example table
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibit 1 (Management Effectiveness) prescribes fields: Submitted By; Area; Fiscal Year; Period From/To; Performance Measurement table listing performance indicators, base period ref (A or B), base year, past year, current year, goals; and a Performance Evaluation narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete each line for performance indicators with base period reference (A = preceding fiscal year cumulative; B = June 30 preceding fiscal year), provide numeric values for base/past/current years, state goals for past and current years, and attach a concise performance evaluation including scope, analysis, accomplishments, problems, and corrective actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency implementation procedures and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency-specific implementation instructions assign responsibilities and set deadlines: Deputy Directors to designate contact officers (example deadline Nov. 10), Directorate plans and reports submitted to Executive Director‑Comptroller by 30 June each year (initial plan for FY1971 submitted by 31 December 1970), and the Director of Planning, Programming, and Budgeting compiles the agency annual report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Agency instructions for submission (format, duplication), designate contact points, and include required attachments and supporting data. Directorate plans must be prepared annually and include the four required sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation responsibility assignment (PP&B)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of Planning, Programming, and Budgeting is responsible for validation of the dollar or other unit value of reported savings and reprogrammings resulting from the Agency's programs prior to preparation of the Agency annual report to the Office of Management and Budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validation consists of reviewing reported actions to confirm accuracy of amounts reported and their disposition/allocation to approved programs; validation procedures should assure reported actions occurred, savings computations are reasonable, and savings are net of offsetting costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-Directorate study inclusion in plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Deputy Directors should include recommendations for inter-Directorate or Agency-wide study areas in their annual plans where such attention is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include suggested scope and rationale for inter-Directorate studies in the Directorate plan so these can be coordinated as Agency or Government-wide special studies via the Bureau of the Budget.
